caption:
The video captures a low-angle view of a clear glass beaker partly filled with liquid, centered on a wooden desk in a classroom setting. A long glass rod leans diagonally into the beaker, and its submerged section appears bent at the waterline because of refraction. Behind it, ceiling panels, fluorescent lights, fans, cabinets, black chairs, and a screen with Korean text remain visible.

The beaker and rod keep the same arrangement, with no pouring, lifting, or repositioning occurring in view. Instead, the framing drifts slowly, shifting the beaker and background slightly downward while the upper-left wall clock becomes progressively more visible. The paper at the desk's left edge remains partly in frame, and the rows of furniture behind the beaker move gradually with the changing viewpoint.

The rod's upper and submerged sections change apparent angle slightly, consistent with perspective shift rather than physical adjustment. The waterline and refracted bend remain visible, and the slow camera drift continues throughout, with the beaker staying near the center of the view.
